nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be coprime integers forming a nondegenerate Lucas pair, and let $(U_n)$ be the Lucas sequence $U(P, Q)$. Then for every $n \ge 1$ with $n \notin \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12, 13, 18, 30\}$, the term $U_n$ has a primitive prime divisor: a prime $p$ that divides $U_n$ but divides no $U_s$ with $1 \le s < n$.
nodes.title: Bilu–Hanrot–Voutier theorem for Lucas sequences

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be coprime integers forming a nondegenerate Lucas pair with discriminant $D = P^2 - 4Q > 0$, and let $(U_n)$ be the Lucas sequence $U(P, Q)$. Then for every $n \ge 1$ with $n \notin \{1, 2, 6, 12\}$, the term $U_n$ has a primitive prime divisor: a prime $p$ that divides $U_n$ but divides no $U_s$ with $1 \le s < n$.
nodes.title: Carmichael's primitive divisor theorem

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be integers with $Q \ne 0$, $P \ne 0$ and $\gcd(P, Q) = 1$, and let $(U_n)$ be the Lucas sequence $U(P, Q)$. If $n$ is a positive integer with $\gcd(n, P) = 1$, then $\gcd(U_{2n}/P, P) = 1$.
nodes.title: Coprimality of $U_{2n}/P$ and $P$

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be coprime integers and let $D = P^2 - 4Q$. Then $\gcd(P, D)$ divides $4$, and $\gcd(P, D') = 1$ for every odd integer $D'$ dividing $D$.
nodes.title: Common divisors of $P$ and the discriminant

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be integers forming a nondegenerate Lucas pair with $Q = \pm 1$, and let $a$ and $b$ be coprime positive integers. Then infinitely many natural numbers $N \equiv b \pmod a$ are Frobenius pseudoprimes with parameters $P$ and $Q$.
nodes.title: Rotkiewicz: Frobenius pseudoprimes in arithmetic progressions

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be integers forming a nondegenerate Lucas pair with $Q = \pm 1$, with $P$ odd if $Q = 1$, and let $(U_n)$ be the Lucas sequence $U(P, Q)$. Call $m$ admissible if it is an odd prime or a Lucas pseudoprime with parameters $P$ and $Q$. Then infinitely many natural numbers $N = |U_{2m}/P|$ with $m$ admissible are both Lucas pseudoprimes and Frobenius pseudoprimes with parameters $P$ and $Q$, and…
nodes.title: Frobenius and non-Frobenius pseudoprimes of the form $U_{2m}/P$

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be integers forming a nondegenerate Lucas pair with $Q = \pm 1$. Then infinitely many products $N = p_1 p_2$ of two distinct odd primes $p_1$ and $p_2$ are both strong Lucas pseudoprimes and Frobenius pseudoprimes with parameters $P$ and $Q$.
nodes.title: Rotkiewicz: strong Lucas and Frobenius pseudoprimes with two prime factors

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q \ne 0$ be integers with discriminant $D = P^2 - 4Q$, and let $(V_n)$ be the companion Lucas sequence $V(P, Q)$. A natural number $N$ is a Dickson pseudoprime of the second kind with parameters $P$ and $Q$ if $N$ is odd, $N > 1$, $N$ is not prime, $\gcd(N, QD) = 1$, and $V_{N - (D/N)} \equiv 2Q^{(1 - (D/N))/2} \pmod N$, where $(D/N)$ is the Jacobi symbol.
nodes.title: Dickson pseudoprimes of the second kind

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q \ne 0$ be integers with discriminant $D = P^2 - 4Q$, and let $(V_n)$ be the companion Lucas sequence $V(P, Q)$. A natural number $N$ is a Dickson pseudoprime with parameters $P$ and $Q$ if $N$ is odd, $N > 1$, $N$ is not prime, $\gcd(N, QD) = 1$, and $V_N \equiv P \pmod N$.
nodes.title: Dickson pseudoprimes

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q \ne 0$ be integers. Every strong Lucas pseudoprime with parameters $P$ and $Q$ is an Euler–Lucas pseudoprime with parameters $P$ and $Q$.

nodes.title: 9 is an Euler–Lucas pseudoprime for P = 1, Q = 5

nodes.summary: Let $U$ and $V$ be the Lucas sequences with integer parameters $P$ and $Q \neq 0$, and let $D = P^2 - 4Q$. A natural number $N$ is an Euler–Lucas pseudoprime with parameters $P, Q$ when $N$ is odd and composite, $\gcd(N, QD) = 1$, and, writing $\varepsilon = (D/N)$ for the Jacobi symbol, $N \mid U_{(N-\varepsilon)/2}$ if the Jacobi symbol $(Q/N)$ equals $1$, and $N \mid V_{(N-\varepsilon)/2}$ if $(Q/N) = -1$.
nodes.title: Euler–Lucas pseudoprime

nodes.summary: The composite number $561 = 3 \cdot 11 \cdot 17$ is an Euler pseudoprime to the base $2$.

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be an integer. A natural number $N$ is an Euler pseudoprime to the base $a$ when $N$ is odd and composite, $\gcd(a, N) = 1$, and $a^{(N-1)/2} \equiv (a/N) \pmod N$, where $(a/N)$ is the Jacobi symbol.
nodes.title: Euler pseudoprime

nodes.summary: For the Lucas sequences with parameters $P = 4$ and $Q = -1$, so that $D = P^2 - 4Q = 20$, the number $9$ is a Frobenius pseudoprime.
nodes.title: 9 is a Frobenius pseudoprime for P = 4, Q = -1

A natural number $N$ is a Frobenius pseudoprime with parameters $P, Q$ when $\gcd(N, PQD) = 1$ and $N$ is a Lucas pseudoprime, a Lucas pseudoprime of the second kind, a Dickson pseudoprime and a Dickson pseudoprime of the second kind with parameters $P, Q$. nodes.title: The rank of appearance in a Lucas sequence is attained

nodes.summary: Let $U = U(P, Q)$ be the Lucas sequence with integer parameters $P$ and $Q \ne 0$. The rank of appearance $\rho(m)$ of a natural number $m$ in $U$ is the least positive integer $r$ with $m \mid U_r$; when no positive $r$ has $m \mid U_r$, $\rho(m) = 0$.

nodes.summary: Let $U = U(P, Q)$ be the Lucas sequence with integer parameters $P$ and $Q \ne 0$, and let $(W_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a sequence of integers with $W_{n+2} = P W_{n+1} - Q W_n$ for every $n \ge 0$. If $t \ge 0$ and $m$ are integers with $m \mid U_t$ and $\gcd(m, Q) = 1$, then $W_{n+t} \equiv U_{t+1} W_n \pmod{m}$ for every $n \ge 0$.

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be integers with $Q \ne 0$, and let $U$ and $V$ be the Lucas sequences $U(P, Q)$ and $V(P, Q)$. Then $P \mid U_{2n}$ for every natural number $n$, and $P \mid V_n$ for every odd natural number $n$.
nodes.title: $P$ divides $U_{2n}$, and $V_n$ for odd $n$

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be coprime integers with $Q \ne 0$, and let $U_n$ be the Lucas sequence $U(P, Q)$. Let $p$ be a prime and $i \ge 1$ such that $p^i \mid P$ and $p^{i+1} \nmid P$. Then for every positive integer $n$, $p^{i+1} \mid U_{2n}$ if and only if $p \mid n$.
nodes.title: When $p^{i+1}$ divides $U_{2n}$, for a prime power $p^i$ exactly dividing $P$

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be integers such that the Lucas pair $(P, Q)$ is nondegenerate, let $D = P^2 - 4Q$, and let $N > 1$ be an odd natural number with $\gcd(N, QD) = 1$. Then $N$ is a Lucas pseudoprime for $(P, Q)$ if and only if it is one for $(-P, Q)$, and the same holds for Lucas pseudoprimes of the second kind, Dickson pseudoprimes, Dickson pseudoprimes of the second kind, and Frobenius pseudoprimes.
nodes.title: Lucas-type pseudoprime properties are unchanged by $P \mapsto -P$
